messages:
emma: heads up — noticed inconsistent routing for /billing when x-env header is present. console shows service=payments-canary but curl to the edge returns payments-stable. anyone seen this? :confused:
raj: saw a similar report yesterday, think it’s the header-override 'greylist' behavior we added. it prefers host specificity unless a header anchor is an exact match. can repro locally.
maria: i can repro too. quick dump of the effected configs below. the header anchor is lower priority than host anchor currently.
maria: ```yaml
- host: "app.redwood.ai"
  path: "/billing/*"
  service: payments-stable
  anchors:
    - header: "x-env=staging"
      service: payments-canary
```
andrew: that YAML is exactly the problem — host match (app.redwood.ai) wins and the header anchor is treated as a tiebreaker only when host specificity ties. our console UX still highlights the header override which is misleading.
sophia: agreed — console should show the final "match reason" (host_specificity | header_anchor | service_alias | fallback). right now we only surface matched route id which hides why we routed to stable vs canary.
linda: from UX standpoint we can add a small pill next to route result: "reason: host_specificity" with a hover explaining precedence. simple and helpful for troubleshooting.
raj: ops side — we should also emit telemetry tags when a header anchor is present but not selected, e.g. tiebreak=host_specificity, anchor_present=true, anchor_key=x-env, anchor_value=staging. that will let us count how often anchors are being ignored.
ops-bot: noted: will add a counter metric route.anchor_ignored with labels {route_id, anchor_key, reason} and alert if > 0.5% of requests for canary routes are ignored over 10m.
deploy-bot: matcher-service v2.14 deployed to canary Thursday, includes greylist heuristics.
emma: small proposal: change precedence so header anchors win when they are explicit equals (x-env=staging) even if host specificity is higher, but only if route has header-anchored rollout flag. that gives teams opt-in control. thoughts?
andrew: opt-in flag sounds reasonable. avoids surprising global behavior changes. name it header_anchor_precedence: optional enum [disabled, opt_in, always]. default opt_in=false.
maria: implementation note: need to update the route canonicalizer and the explainable-match API. add a new field in the match response: match_reason (string) and match_path (list) for telemetry.
sophia: console change: show match_reason in trace panel and add a quick "why this route?" toggle that expands the decision chain (host -> path -> headers -> fallback). we can ship a minimal pill first then expand.
emma: action items: raj to draft precedence RFC for header_anchor_precedence, andrew to sketch minimal API change (match_reason + match_path), linda to mock UI pill. ship window 2 weeks for the telemetry + UI pill, RFC out for review EOD tomorrow.
raj: starting RFC draft now. will include perf implications (extra header checks per-match) and rollout plan.
ops-bot: FYI: adding metrics may spike cardinality; recommend anchor_key/value sampling for high-card routes.
emma: good call. raj add sampling guidance in RFC. thanks all :thumbsup:
